anchors.extracted: Cutoffs define the concentrations needed for a positive result; a result below the cutoff is reported as negative, which means the concentration was lower than the cutoff, not that the substance was absent. Laboratories may use cutoffs that differ from the federal ones, which were set for adults in the workplace; lower cutoffs reduce false negatives but may increase false positives. Federal workplace cutoffs (Table 1), screen then confirmation (ng/mL): marijuana metabolites 50, then THCCOOH 15; cocaine metabolites 150, then benzoylecgonine 100; codeine/morphine 2000 and 2000; 6-acetylmorphine 10 and 10; phencyclidine 25 and 25; amphetamine/methamphetamine 500, then 250 each; MDMA 500, then MDMA, MDA and MDEA 250 each.

anchors.extracted: Screening immunoassays for cannabis react to several THC metabolites (federal cutoff 50 ng/mL; some laboratories use 20 ng/mL); confirmation by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS is specific for THCCOOH, with a federal cutoff of 15 ng/mL. Detection depends on route, amount and potency, frequency of use, body mass and metabolic rate; chronic use leads to THC accumulating in fat and slow elimination, so cannabis can be detected in urine for more than 30 days after stopping in people who used chronically, whereas a single exposure in people who do not use it is typically detectable for up to 72 hours.
